title: RELIEF-Study: REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE ON HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE AND EFFECTIVENESS OF RUXOLITINIB CREAM IN MODERATE ATOPIC DERMATITIS IN ROUTINE GERMAN PRACTICE
summary:
Background
 Atopic dermatitis, also known as eczema, is a common long-term skin condition that can cause intense itching, redness, and recurring skin symptoms. These symptoms can have a significant impact on daily life and well-being. A new cream treatment called Opzelura® (ruxolitinib cream) is available for adults with moderate atopic dermatitis.

Research Question
 The purpose of this study is to evaluate how well treatment with ruxolitinib cream works under routine medical care conditions. In particular, the study will assess changes in skin symptoms and itching over time during treatment.

Methods
 This is a non-interventional study. The decision to prescribe ruxolitinib cream is made by the treating physician independently of study participation. No additional medical procedures or interventions are required as part of the study. Participants will complete questionnaires during their regular clinic visits and record information about their symptoms in an electronic diary. Approximately 660 adults from around 100 dermatology practices and clinics across Germany are expected to take part. Each participant will be followed for up to 24 months. The results will help improve understanding of how this treatment performs in everyday clinical practice.

interventions.name: Adult patients with moderate atopic dermatitis receiving routine treatment with Opzelura® (ruxolitinib) cream, with follow-up of up to 2 years.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients with a physician-reported diagnosis of moderate AD in adult patients for whom topical corticosteroids (TCS) and topical calcineurin inhibitors (TCI) are inadequate or inappropriate
• The decision upon treatment with Opzelura® (ruxolitinib) cream must have been made before enrollment and independently of this non-interventional observational study
• Patient is at least 18 years of age at the time of treatment decision
• Patient provided written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
All contraindications according to the approved Opzelura® (ruxolitinib) cream summary of product characteristics (SmPC), i.e., hypersensitivity to any of the components of ruxolitinib cream, pregnancy, and breastfeeding.
